content:
I have been asked to advertise this: the CNRS (French National Centre for Scientific Research) wants to open a CPJ (= Chaire de Professeur Junior) this year on the topic "Generative AI for formal proofs". They are waiting for confirmation from higher levels but want to start spreading the word.

This is a tenure-track position. After 3 to 6 years, the person holding the position gets a tenure review and, if they are successful, they become a CNRS senior researcher (with tenure, and with no teaching duties). It is expected that the success rate at tenure reviews will be high, but the positions are very new, and the first tenure reviews have not taken place yet.

The conditions of the position are the following:

  • It is based in Lyon, either at UMPA (the math department of the ENS de Lyon), LIP (the computer science department of the ENS de Lyon) or ICJ (the math department of the Université Lyon 1+Université Saint-Étienne);
  • You need a PhD to apply, and ideally some post-PhD experience;
  • Salary will be around 55 000 euro a year before taxes (depending on experience level);
  • There is a startup package of 200 000 euro.
  • There is teaching, around 45 hours of lecturing a year (or 64 hours of exercise sessions). It's typically graduate teaching and can be done in English.

The CNRS expects that applications will be open between July 15 and September 1 (2026!), the selection process (including interviews) will take place during the fall, and the position will start at the end of 2026, with deferrals being possible until February 2027.

If you are interested, you should contact at least one of the three departments: UMPA (https://www.umpa.ens-lyon.fr/), LIP (https://www.ens-lyon.fr/LIP/), ICJ (https://math.univ-lyon1.fr/icj/). Ideally, find people you could be working with and write to them.

If you have questions about the position and/or the process, you can ask here or send a DM to @Sophie Morel . She is on a lot of CNRS committees but will not be on the one for this position, so she has some information about the process and is allowed to answer questions.

By the way, I should mention that there is a second CNRS position (also tenure-track, same conditions as the one above) in number theory/arithmetic geometry, and it explicitly mentions formalized mathematics in that field as part of its scope:
"The chair's research themes intersect with numerous fields of mathematics, including algebra, analysis, computer science, geometry, cryptography, coding theory, dynamical systems, and more. These themes are intended to encompass the entire spectrum of number theory and arithmetic geometry. They may also, where appropriate, address aspects of formalized mathematics related to the field."
That position will be based in Caen, Clermont or Strasbourg. If you're interested, you should contact people in one of these places.

The deadline to apply is also September 2 at 5pm, and the link is there:
https://emploi.cnrs.fr/Offres/CPJ/CPJ-2026-006/Default.aspx?lang=EN
